''[[Battlestar Galactica (2004 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]'' is an American [[military science fiction]] [[television series]], and part of the [[Battlestar Galactica|''Battlestar Galactica'' franchise]]. The show was developed by [[Ronald D. Moore]] as a re-imagining of the 1978 [[Battlestar Galactica (1978 TV series)|''Battlestar Galactica'']] television series created by [[Glen A. Larson]]. The series first aired as a [[Battlestar Galactica (miniseries)|three-hour miniseries]] (comprising four broadcast hours) in December 2003 on the [[Syfy|Sci-Fi Channel]]. The television series debuted in the United Kingdom on [[Sky1]] on October 18, 2004, and premiered in the United States on the Sci-Fi Channel on January 14, 2005.

The [[story arc]] of ''Battlestar Galactica'' is set in a distant star system, where a civilization of humans live on a series of planets known as the [[Twelve Colonies of Kobol]]. In the past, the Colonies had been at war with a cybernetic race of their own creation, known as the [[Cylon (re-imagining)|Cylon]]s. With the self-serving and venal help of a human named [[Gaius Baltar]], the Cylons, some now in human form, launch a sudden [[sneak attack]] on the Colonies, laying waste to the planets and devastating their populations. Out of a population numbering in the billions, only approximately 50,000 humans survive, most of whom were aboard civilian [[Spacecraft|spaceships]] that avoided destruction. Of all the Colonial Fleet, the eponymous [[Battlestar Galactica (ship)|battlestar ''Galactica'']] appears to be the only military capital ship that survived the attack. Under the leadership of Colonial Fleet officer [[William Adama|Commander William "Bill" Adama]] and President [[Laura Roslin]], the ''Galactica'' and its crew take up the task of leading the small fugitive fleet of survivors into space in search of a fabled refuge known as [[Earth]].

==Episodes==
===Miniseries (2003)===
{{main|Battlestar Galactica (miniseries)}}
{{Episode table |background=#990033 |title=32 |director=19 |writer=21 |aux1=9 |airdate=18 |aux1T=Survivor<br>count |episodes={{Episode list
| Title           = Part/Night 1
| Aux1            = {{TableTBA|Unspecified}}
| DirectedBy      = [[Michael Rymer]]
| WrittenBy       = [[Ronald D. Moore]] and [[Glen A. Larson|Christopher Eric James]]
| OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2003|12|08}}
| ShortSummary    = Secretary of Education [[Laura Roslin]] visits the [[Battlestar Galactica (fictional spacecraft)|Battlestar ''Galactica'']] for its decommissioning ceremony. The [[Cylon (reimagining)|Cylon]]s launch a surprise [[Nuclear weapon|nuclear]]-attack on the [[Twelve Colonies of Kobol]], ending a 40-year [[armistice]] between the Cylons and humans; most of the human population is wiped out, and the majority of the human fleet is destroyed due to [[malware]] implanted by the Cylons. ''Galactica'' survives, and its commander, [[William Adama]], assumes command of the human fleet. Roslin aboard a Colonial passenger ship survives as well, and is sworn in as the President of the Twelve Colonies after most of the government have been killed. Roslin orders to start rescuing civilian ships, while Adama, on the contrary, orders all ships to regroup at Ragnar Station for counterattack-preparations. A shuttle from ''Galactica'', crewed by [[Sharon Valerii|Sharon "Boomer" Valerii]] and [[Karl Agathon|Karl "Helo" Agathon]], lands briefly on the human capital-world of Caprica after escaping the fight with the Cylons; Helo switches places with [[Gaius Baltar]], a renowned human scientist who unknowingly helped the Cylons gain access into the human military-computers; Boomer, Baltar and a few more survivors leave Caprica, while Helo is left behind. As the Cylons attack ''Colonial One'', the ship appears to be destroyed by a nuclear explosion.
| LineColor       = 990033
}}
{{Episode list
| Title           = Part/Night 2
| Aux1            = 50,298
| DirectedBy      = Michael Rymer
| WrittenBy       = Ronald D. Moore and Christopher Eric James
| OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2003|12|09}}
| ShortSummary    = Adama orders ''Galactica'' to jump to Ragnar Station using [[faster-than-light]] (FTL) technology; aboard, they find a man named [[Leoben Conoy|Leoben]], who is revealed to be a [[Humanoid Cylons|humanoid Cylon model]], and is killed by Adama. ''Colonial One'' is revealed to be intact; Adama's son [[Lee Adama|Lee]] had used [[Electromagnetic pulse|EMP]] generators on board to simulate the ship's destruction and engineer its escape from the Cylons. Boomer and Baltar reach ''Colonial One''. The Cylons discover Roslin's grown fleet of civilian ships; she orders all FTL-equipped ships to jump to Ragnar, abandoning the rest. Roslin's fleet joins ''Galactica''. Baltar is haunted by a virtual image of the female humanoid Cylon model, "[[Number Six (Battlestar Galactica)|Number Six]]." He fabricates evidence against another civilian, [[Aaron Doral]], thinking he is another Cylon model; Doral is arrested. Roslin convinces Adama to stop counterattack preparations, and instead focus on humanity's survival. ''Galactica'' and the civilian fleet leave the star system after the battle with the Cylons, leaving Doral on Ragnar. Adama promises the crew to take them to the scriptural planet known as "[[Earth in science fiction|Earth]]." Doral is confirmed to be a Cylon, as multiple copies of him, Six, and Leoben meet on Ragnar; another Cylon model is revealed to look exactly like Boomer.
| LineColor       = 990033
}}
}}

The film reveals the chronicles of the Battlestar ''Pegasus'' and its crew from the initial Cylon attack on the Twelve Colonies, up to its meeting with ''Galactica'', while Apollo's new [[Executive Officer|XO]] deals with the harsh reality of Admiral Cain's legacy.

| WrittenBy       = [[Jane Espenson]]
| OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2009|10|27}} (Blu-ray/DVD)<br />{{Start date|2010|01|10}} (TV)
| ShortSummary    = The film provides an alternate perspective on many events already known to the viewer. Chronologically, this takes place throughout seasons 1 and 2 only (and the miniseries), but contains plot revelations of the entire series.

As two [[John Cavil]] Cylons wait to be blown out of a ''Galactica'' airlock, they discuss their opposing opinions on the plan to annihilate humankind. They reflect on their own experiences with the humans since the attack on the Twelve Colonies, their roles in the orchestration of the Cylon agents onboard the ''Galactica'', and efforts to sabotage the resistance effort on Caprica come to light.
| LineColor       = 4B0082

'''Notes:'''

#{{note|1}} In addition to the [[Blu-ray Disc]] releases, this set was also released on [[HD DVD]], on December 4, 2007.<ref name=dvd_tvshowsondvd_r1/>
#{{note|2}} ''Razor'', though being a television movie, is considered to be the first two episodes of season 4, hence the fourth season is technically 22 episodes and runs from 2007 to 2009.
#{{note|3}} This set does not contain the second half of Season 4, also known as ''The Final Season''.
#{{note|4}} This set does not contain ''The Plan''.
#{{note|5}} This set also contains the complete 1978 ''[[Battlestar Galactica (1978 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]'' series, including ''[[Galactica 1980]]''.
#{{note|6}} This set also contains ''[[Battlestar Galactica: Blood & Chrome]]'', the complete ''[[Caprica (TV series)|Caprica]]'' series, the complete 1978 ''[[Battlestar Galactica (1978 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]'' series, the complete ''[[Galactica 1980]]'' series, and the [[Saga of a Star World|1978 feature film based on the original series pilot episode]]. This set has been released in European French speaking countries only.

== Online availability ==
In January 2006, [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] began offering the episodes for the miniseries, season 1, and season 2 for purchase on the U.S. version of the [[iTunes Store]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2005/12/22/sci-fi-inside-battlestar-galactica-to-premiere-on-the-itunes-music-store-20159/20051222scifi01/|title=Sci Fi Inside: Battlestar Galactica' to Premiere on the iTunes Music Store|publisher=Sci Fi|date=December 22, 2005 |access-date=July 13, 2011 }}</ref> In December 2007, the ''Battlestar Galactica'' episodes were removed from iTunes, along with other NBC Universal content.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tech.fortune.cnn.com/2007/12/03/nbc-pulls-its-tv-shows-from-apple-itunes/|title=NBC pulls its TV shows from Apple iTunes|website=Fortune Tech|date=December 3, 2007 |access-date=July 13, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515220011/http://tech.fortune.cnn.com/2007/12/03/nbc-pulls-its-tv-shows-from-apple-itunes/|archive-date=May 15, 2012 |url-status=dead |first= Philip |last=Elmer-DeWitt }}</ref> In September 2008, the episodes returned to iTunes when NBC Universal announced their return to iTunes.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2008/09/09/nbc-universal-returns-to-the-itunes-store--28735/20080909nbc03/|title=NBC Universal Returns to the iTunes Store|publisher=NBC|date=September 9, 2008 |access-date=July 13, 2011 |author=The Futon Critic}}</ref> In February 2009, the series became available in [[High-definition video|high-definition]] format at the UK iTunes Store.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.igizmo.co.uk/articles/news/978-home-entertainment-hd-revolution-gathers-pace-uk-itunes-store|title=HD revolution gathers pace in UK iTunes Store|date=February 6, 2009 |access-date=February 6, 2009 |website=iGizmo|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219042118/http://www.igizmo.co.uk/articles/news/978-home-entertainment-hd-revolution-gathers-pace-uk-itunes-store |archive-date=February 19, 2012 |last=James |first=Martin }}</ref>

The series has also been available via [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.syfy.com/syfy-wire/all-four-seasons-of-battlestar-galactica-streaming-on-peacock-right-now|title=Blast off with all four seasons of 'Battlestar Galactica' - streaming on Peacock|publisher=Syfy|date=March 13, 2023 |access-date=May 19, 2023 }}</ref> [[Amazon Video]],<ref>{{cite press In September 2020, the series was made available on the [[BBC iPlayer]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Acclaimed science fiction series Battlestar Galactica coming to BBC iPlayer |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/latestnews/2020/battlestar-galactica |publisher=BBC |date=August 26, 2020 |access-date=May 17, 2026}}</ref> On May 1, 2026, the entire series–including the miniseries and the television film ''The Plan''– were added to [[Paramount+]] and [[Pluto TV]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.paramountplus.com/sneak-peak/how-to-watch-battlestar-galactica-on-paramount-plus/ |title=How To Watch The Battlestar Galactica Franchise On Paramount+ |website=Paramount+ |first=Doriean |last=Stevenson |date=May 1, 2026 |access-date=May 17, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/2155005/battlestar-galactica-sci-fi-franchise-streaming-paramount-plus-pluto-tv/ |title=Battlestar Galactica, Caprica, And More Franchise Titles To Stream On Paramount+ And Pluto TV |website=TVLine |first=Andy |last=Swift |date=April 23, 2026 |access-date=May 17, 2026}}</ref>
